significance: A late 18th-century Dravidian temple to Narasimha built over roughly a decade by three brothers, sons of Kacheri Krishnappa, a Dewan under Tipu Sultan. It has a three-tiered gopura, a prakara wall and open and closed mantapas.
story: B. Lewis Rice records that a merchant's pot of grain turned blood-red when boiled on a sacred rock here, and that the god appeared in his dream asking that a temple be raised in atonement.
